📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough This PR removes the batch-based skiplist name management abstractions. Specifically deleted are the `NameBatch` type with its name storage/manipulation and serialization methods, the `NameList` type with batch-based insertion/deletion/iteration logic, associated serialization functions, and their unit tests. The protobuf `NameBatchData` message definition is also removed from the schema. ## Changes **NameBatch and NameList Abstraction Removal** | Layer / File(s) | Summary | |---|---| | **Proto message definition removal**
`weed/util/skiplist/skiplist.proto` | `NameBatchData` protobuf message is removed from the skiplist schema, eliminating the serialized batch format used by the now-deleted NameBatch and NameList implementations. | ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 1 (Trivial) | ⏱️ ~5 minutes ## Poem > A skiplist once held batches with care, > NameBatch and NameList danced there, > But now they fade away, > Proto messages say goodbye today, > The abstraction vanishes into air. 🐰

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
